title.zh: 卷一百九十二 志第一百四十五 兵六
title.raw: 卷一百九十二 志第一百四十五 兵六 Volume 192 Treatises 145: Military 6

sentences.zh: 兵六

translations.literal: Military 6
translations.idiomatic: Military 6

sentences.zh: （鄉兵三）〉

translations.literal: (Local Militia 3)
translations.idiomatic: (Local Militia 3)

sentences.zh: ○保甲建炎後鄉兵建炎後砦兵

translations.literal: ○ Baojia; Local Militia after the Jianyan era; Fortress Troops after the Jianyan era
translations.idiomatic: ○ Baojia; local militia after the Jianyan era; fortress troops after the Jianyan era

sentences.zh: 保甲熙寧初，王安石變募兵而行保甲，帝從其議。

translations.literal: Baojia: At the beginning of the Xining reign, Wang Anshi changed from hired troops to implementing baojia, and the emperor followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Baojia. At the outset of the Xining reforms, Wang Anshi replaced the system of hired troops with the baojia militia, and the emperor adopted his plan.

sentences.zh: 三年，始聯比其民以相保任。

translations.literal: In the third year, the people were first linked in groups for mutual guarantee and responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, the populace was first organized into linked groups bound to guarantee one another.

sentences.zh: 及詔畿內之民十家為一保，選主戶有幹力者一人為保長。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered that within the Capital District ten households form one bao, selecting one capable head-of-household as bao chief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then required that within the metropolitan region ten households form one bao, with one capable principal householder chosen as bao chief.

sentences.zh: 五十家為一大保，選一人為大保長。

translations.literal: Fifty households formed one large bao, and one person was selected as large-bao chief.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty households made up one large bao, and one man was chosen as its chief.

sentences.zh: 十大保為一都保，選為眾所服者為都保正，又以一人為之副。

translations.literal: Ten large bao formed one du-bao; the one whom the multitude obeyed was chosen as du-bao head, and another person served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Ten large bao formed one supervisory du-bao; the man most respected in the community became du-bao head, with a deputy appointed beside him.

sentences.zh: 應主客戶兩丁以上，選一人為保丁。

translations.literal: From each host or client household with two adult males or more, one was selected as a bao ding.
translations.idiomatic: From every host or tenant household with at least two adult males, one was selected to serve as a bao ding.

sentences.zh: 附保。

translations.literal: They were attached to the bao.
translations.idiomatic: Such persons were registered with the bao.

sentences.zh: 兩丁以上有餘丁而壯勇者亦附之。

translations.literal: Households with more than two males who had surplus males who were strong and brave were also attached.
translations.idiomatic: Households with more than two males also enrolled any extra sons who were strong and valiant.

sentences.zh: 內家貲最厚、材勇過人者亦充保丁，兵器非禁者聽習。

translations.literal: Within the bao, those with the greatest household wealth and martial talent surpassing others also served as bao ding; they were permitted to practice with weapons not prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Within each bao, men of the greatest wealth and outstanding courage also served as bao ding and were allowed to drill with weapons not forbidden by law.

sentences.zh: 每一大保夜輪五人警盜。

translations.literal: Each large bao nightly rotated five men to guard against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Each large bao took turns sending five men each night to watch for thieves.

sentences.zh: 凡告捕所獲，以賞格從事。

translations.literal: For all apprehensions through reporting, rewards were granted according to the reward schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards for successful reports and captures followed the official bounty schedule.

sentences.zh: 同保犯強盜、殺人、放火、強奸、略人、傳習妖教、造畜蠱毒，知而不告，依律伍保法。

translations.literal: If members of the same bao committed robbery, murder, arson, rape, abduction, studied heterodox teachings, or manufactured gu poison, and others knew but did not report, they were punished under the law of mutual responsibility among five bao.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone in the same bao committed robbery, murder, arson, rape, abduction, the study of heterodox cults, or the manufacture of gu poison, and others knew but failed to report it, they were punished under the mutual-responsibility law binding five bao together.

sentences.zh: 餘事非幹己，又非敕律所聽糾，皆毋得告，雖知情亦不坐。

translations.literal: For other matters not concerning oneself and not subject to denunciation under edicts and statutes, no report was permitted; even if one knew, there was no punishment.
translations.idiomatic: For all other matters that did not concern oneself and were not subject to denunciation under edict or statute, no report was allowed; even knowledge brought no penalty.

sentences.zh: 若於法鄰保合坐罪者乃坐之。

translations.literal: Only when neighboring bao were liable to share punishment under the law were they punished.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring bao were punished only when the law made them jointly liable.

sentences.zh: 其居停強盜三人，經三日，保鄰雖不知情，科失覺罪。

translations.literal: If three robbers lodged with a household for three days, the bao and neighbors, though ignorant, were punished for failure to detect.
translations.idiomatic: If three robbers lodged in a household for three days, the bao and neighbors were punished for failure to detect them even if they had not known.

sentences.zh: 逃移、死絕、同保不及五家，並他保。

translations.literal: Flight, relocation, death so that a bao had fewer than five households—all were merged into other bao.
translations.idiomatic: When households fled, moved away, or died off so that a bao fell below five households, it was merged into another bao.

sentences.zh: 有自外入保者，收為同保，戶數足則附之，俟及十家，則別為保，置牌以書其戶數姓名。

translations.literal: Outsiders entering a bao were received into the same bao; when the household count was sufficient they were attached; when ten households accumulated, a separate bao was formed, and a plaque recorded household count and names.
translations.idiomatic: Outsiders who entered a bao were enrolled in it; when the quota was filled they were attached, and when ten households had gathered a new bao was formed and a plaque inscribed with household count and names.

sentences.zh: 既行之畿甸，遂推之五路，以達於天下。

translations.literal: After it was implemented in the Capital District, it was extended to the Five Circuits and throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Once the system was in place in the metropolitan region, it was extended to the Five Circuits and then to the whole empire.

sentences.zh: 時則以捕盜賊相保任，而未肄以武事也。

translations.literal: At that time mutual guarantee was used to apprehend bandits, but martial training had not yet been instituted.
translations.idiomatic: At that stage the system served chiefly to guarantee one another in catching bandits; martial drill had not yet been introduced.

sentences.zh: 四年，始詔畿內保丁肄習武事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict first ordered Capital District bao ding to practice martial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year an edict first ordered the bao ding of the metropolitan region to train in martial skills.

sentences.zh: 歲農隙，所隸官期日於要便鄉村都試騎步射，並以射中親疏遠近為等。

translations.literal: During agricultural slack seasons, supervising officials on set dates at convenient rural sites conducted mounted and foot archery tests, grading by hits at various distances.
translations.idiomatic: During the agricultural off-season, supervising officials on fixed days held mounted and foot archery trials at convenient rural sites, ranking contestants by hits at varying distances.

sentences.zh: 騎射校其用馬，有餘藝而願試者聽。

translations.literal: Mounted archery was also judged on horsemanship; those with additional skills who wished to test were allowed.
translations.idiomatic: In mounted archery horsemanship was also assessed, and those with further skills who wished to compete were permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 第一等保明以聞，天子親閱試之，命以官使。

translations.literal: First-rank achievers were reported by the bao to the throne; the emperor personally reviewed them and appointed them to office.
translations.idiomatic: First-rank men were reported by their bao to the court; the emperor personally examined them and granted official appointments.

sentences.zh: 第二等免當年春夫一月，馬槁四十，役錢二千。

translations.literal: Second rank: exemption from one month of spring corvée, forty bundles of horse fodder, two thousand cash in service fees.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank brought exemption from one month of spring corvée labor, forty bundles of horse fodder, and two thousand cash in service fees.

sentences.zh: 本戶無可免，或所免不及，聽移免他戶而受其直。

translations.literal: If the household had nothing to exempt or the exemption was insufficient, another household could receive the benefit in exchange for payment.
translations.idiomatic: If the household had nothing to exempt or the exemption fell short, the benefit could be transferred to another household in return for payment.

sentences.zh: 第三、第四等視此有差。

translations.literal: Third and fourth ranks had proportionally reduced rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Third and fourth ranks received proportionally smaller rewards.

sentences.zh: 藝未精願候閱試，或附甲單丁願就閱試者，並聽。

translations.literal: Those whose skill was not yet refined who wished to await review, or single males attached to a bao who wished to test, were all permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Those whose skill was not yet sufficient but who wished to wait for another review, and unattached single males who wished to compete, were all allowed.

sentences.zh: 都副保正武藝雖不及等，而能整齊保戶無擾，勸誘丁壯習藝及等，捕盜比他保最多，弭盜比他保最少，所隸官以聞，其恩視第一等焉。

translations.literal: Du-bao heads and deputies whose martial skill did not reach a grade but who could keep households orderly without disturbance, encourage young men to train to grade, catch more bandits than other bao, and quell theft better—the supervising official reported this; their rewards were like the first grade.
translations.idiomatic: Du-bao heads and deputies whose own martial skill fell short of a grade but who kept their households orderly, urged young men to reach standard, caught more bandits and suppressed theft better than other bao were reported by the supervising official and received rewards equal to the first grade.

sentences.zh: 都副保正有闕，選大保長充。

translations.literal: When du-bao head or deputy positions were vacant, large-bao chiefs were selected to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: Vacancies among du-bao heads and deputies were filled by selecting large-bao chiefs.

sentences.zh: 都副保正雖勸誘丁壯習藝，而輒強率妨務者，禁之。

translations.literal: Du-bao heads and deputies who encouraged training but forcibly conscripted and obstructed productive work were forbidden from doing so.
translations.idiomatic: Du-bao heads and deputies who urged young men to train but forcibly conscripted them and interfered with their regular work were forbidden to do so.

sentences.zh: 吏因保甲事受賕、斂掠，加乞取監臨三等，仗、徒、編管、配隸，告者次第賞之，命官犯者除名。

translations.literal: Officials who took bribes or extorted in baojia matters faced penalties three grades harsher than supervisory corruption—flogging, penal servitude, registration, exile; informants received graduated rewards; commissioned officials were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who accepted bribes or extorted in baojia matters were punished three grades more severely than for ordinary supervisory corruption—with flogging, penal servitude, registration, or exile; informants received graduated rewards, and commissioned officials were stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 時雖使之習武技而未番上也。

translations.literal: At the time they were made to practice martial skills but not yet assigned rotating duty.
translations.idiomatic: At that time they were trained in martial skills but were not yet placed on rotating duty.

sentences.zh: 五年，右正言、知制誥、判司農寺曾布言：“近日保戶數以狀詣縣，願分番隸巡檢司習武技，提點司以聞朝廷及司農寺，未敢輒議，願下提點司送中書詳審，付司農具為令。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Right Remonstrator, Drafter, and Acting Director of the Bureau of Agriculture Zeng Bu said: "Recently bao households in numbers petitioned the county wishing to rotate in batches under the patrol office to practice martial skills; the intendant circuit reported this to the court and the Bureau of Agriculture but did not dare decide on his own. He asked that the intendant circuit send the matter to the Secretariat for detailed review and that the Bureau of Agriculture draft regulations."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Zeng Bu, Right Remonstrator, drafter, and acting director of the Bureau of Agriculture, said: "Recently many bao households have petitioned the county asking to drill in rotating shifts under the patrol office. The intendant circuit has reported this to the court and to our bureau but has not dared to decide alone. I ask that the intendant circuit forward the matter to the Secretariat for review and that the Bureau of Agriculture draw up regulations."

sentences.zh: ”於是詔：“主戶保丁願上番於巡檢司，十日一更，疾故者次番代之。

translations.literal: "An edict then ordered: "Host-household bao ding who wished to rotate duty at the patrol office changed every ten days; those ill or deceased were replaced in the next rotation."
translations.idiomatic: "Thereupon an edict declared: "Principal-household bao ding who wished to serve rotating shifts at the patrol office would change every ten days; the sick or deceased would be replaced in the next rotation."

sentences.zh: 月給口糧、薪菜錢，分番巡警，每五十人輪大保長二、都副保正一統領之。

translations.literal: Monthly grain rations and fuel and vegetable money were issued; they patrolled in rotating shifts, with every fifty men led in rotation by two large-bao chiefs and one du-bao head or deputy.
translations.idiomatic: They received monthly grain rations and allowances for fuel and vegetables, patrolled in rotating shifts, and every fifty men were led in turn by two large-bao chiefs and one du-bao head or deputy.

sentences.zh: 都副保正月各給錢七千，大保長三千。

translations.literal: Du-bao heads and deputies each received seven thousand cash per month; large-bao chiefs three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Du-bao heads and deputies each received seven thousand cash a month, and large-bao chiefs three thousand.

sentences.zh: 當番者毋得輒離本所。

translations.literal: Those on duty were not permitted to leave their post without authorization.
translations.idiomatic: Men on active rotation were not to leave their station without permission.

sentences.zh: 捕逐劇盜，雖下番人亦聽追集，給其錢斛，事訖遣還，毋過上番人數，仍折除其上番日。

translations.literal: In pursuing major bandits, even men off rotation were allowed to be assembled, given grain and cash, and sent back when done; they were not to exceed the number on duty, and their days on duty were deducted accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: In pursuing serious bandits, even men off rotation could be called up, supplied with grain and cash, and dismissed when the affair was concluded; their number was not to exceed those on duty, and equivalent days were deducted from their rotation.

sentences.zh: 巡檢司量留廂界給使，餘兵悉罷。

translations.literal: The patrol office retained only as many men as needed for its district; the rest were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The patrol office kept only as many troops as its district required; the remainder were all disbanded.

sentences.zh: 應番保丁武技及第三等已上，並記於籍。

translations.literal: All rotating bao ding with martial skill of third grade and above were recorded in the register.
translations.idiomatic: All rotating bao ding who reached third grade or higher in martial skill were entered in the register.

sentences.zh: 遇歲凶，五分已上者第振之，自十五石至三石為差。

translations.literal: In years of famine, those who had lost half or more of their crop were relieved in grades from fifteen piculs down to three.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years those who had lost half or more of their harvest were relieved in stages, from fifteen piculs down to three.

sentences.zh: ”十一月，又詔尉司上番保丁如巡檢司法。

translations.literal: "In the eleventh month, another edict ordered that rotating bao ding under the constable's office follow the same law as under the patrol office.
translations.idiomatic: "In the eleventh month another edict required rotating bao ding under the constable's office to follow the same rules as those under the patrol office.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔開封府畿以都保置木契，左留司農寺，右付其縣，凡追胥、閱試、肄習則出契。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered that the Capital District establish wooden tallies for each du-bao, the left copy kept at the Bureau of Agriculture, the right given to the county; for pursuit, review, and drill the tally was produced.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year an edict required the metropolitan region to issue wooden tallies for each du-bao, one copy kept at the Bureau of Agriculture and one given to the county; the tally was produced whenever men were called out for pursuit, review, or drill.

sentences.zh: 是月，又詔行於永興、秦鳳、河北東西、河東五路，唯毋上番。

translations.literal: That month, another edict extended the system to the Yongxing, Qinfeng, Hebei East and West, and Hedong circuits, but without rotating duty.
translations.idiomatic: That same month another edict extended the system to the Yongxing, Qinfeng, eastern and western Hebei, and Hedong circuits, but without rotating duty.

sentences.zh: 餘路止相保任，毋習武藝，內荊湖、川、廣並邊者可肄武事，令監司度之。

translations.literal: Other circuits only mutual guarantee, no martial training; within Jinghu, Sichuan, Guang, and border regions martial affairs might be practiced, left to the judgment of circuit supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Other circuits were limited to mutual guarantee without martial drill; within Jinghu, Sichuan, Guang, and the border regions martial training might be permitted at the discretion of circuit supervisors.

sentences.zh: 後惟全、邵土丁、邕、欽洞丁、廣東槍手改為保甲者則肄焉。

translations.literal: Later only native soldiers of Quan and Shao, cave soldiers of Yong and Qin, and Guangdong musketeers converted to baojia practiced martial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later only the native levies of Quan and Shao, the cave soldiers of Yong and Qin, and Guangdong musketeers reorganized as baojia received martial training.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乃罷河北西路強壯、緣邊弓箭社係籍番上巡守者。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the registered rotating border patrol of strong men and frontier archer societies of Hebei West Circuit was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the registered rotating border patrol of strong men and frontier archer societies in western Hebei was abolished.

sentences.zh: 初，開封府畿、五路保甲及五萬人，二年一解發，詣京師閱試命官，開封府畿十人，五路七人。

translations.literal: Initially, for every fifty thousand baojia in the Capital District and Five Circuits, one man every two years was sent to the capital for review and appointment: ten from the Capital District, seven from the Five Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: At first, for every fifty thousand baojia in the metropolitan region and the Five Circuits, one man every two years was sent to the capital for review and appointment—ten from the metropolitan region and seven from the Five Circuits.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔開封府畿及一萬人、五路及一萬五千人，各許解發一人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict allowed one man per ten thousand in the Capital District and per fifteen thousand in the Five Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year an edict allowed one man to be sent for every ten thousand in the metropolitan region and for every fifteen thousand in the Five Circuits.

sentences.zh: 九年，樞密院請自今都副保正、義勇軍校二年一比選，縣考其訓習武藝及等最多、捕察而盜賊最少者上於州，州上所轄官司，同比較以聞。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the Bureau of Military Affairs requested that henceforth du-bao heads and deputies and yiyong company officers be compared every two years; the county examined who trained the most to grade and caught the most bandits with the fewest thefts and reported to the prefecture, which reported to superior offices for joint comparison.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Bureau of Military Affairs asked that du-bao heads and deputies and yiyong company officers be compared every two years; counties would nominate those who trained the most men to standard and caught the most bandits with the fewest thefts, prefectures would forward the lists, and superior offices would compare them and report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 或中選人多，則擇武藝最優者。

translations.literal: If many were selected, the one with the finest martial skill was chosen.
translations.idiomatic: When many qualified, the man of the highest martial skill was chosen.

sentences.zh: 額外尚有可解發者，則第其次為之旌勸。

translations.literal: If beyond the quota others could still be sent, those next in rank received commendation.
translations.idiomatic: If additional men beyond the quota merited dispatch, those next in rank received commendation and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 第一次，州縣籍記姓名，犯杖以下聽贖；

translations.literal: The first time, prefectures and counties recorded their names; offenses punishable by flogging or less could be redeemed;
translations.idiomatic: The first time, prefectures and counties recorded their names on the register, and offenses punishable by flogging or less could be redeemed;

sentences.zh: 第二次，以等第賜杖子、紫衫、銀帶，犯徒罪情輕奏裁；

translations.literal: the second time, by grade they were given staffs, purple robes, and silver belts; minor penal offenses were submitted for imperial decision;
translations.idiomatic: the second time they received staffs, purple robes, and silver belts according to grade, and minor penal offenses were submitted for imperial decision;

sentences.zh: 累及三次者，降宣補之，給馬及芻菽。

translations.literal: those who reached three times received edict appointments, horses, and fodder.
translations.idiomatic: those who reached a third selection received edict appointments, horses, and fodder.

sentences.zh: 五路義勇軍校二千，解發毋得過三人。

translations.literal: For every two thousand yiyong company officers in the Five Circuits, no more than three could be sent.
translations.idiomatic: For every two thousand yiyong company officers in the Five Circuits, no more than three could be sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 保甲都副保正之解發者亦以二年，府界六人，河北、河東各四人，永興、秦鳳等路七人。

translations.literal: Baojia du-bao heads and deputies sent every two years: six from the metropolitan region, four each from Hebei and Hedong, seven from Yongxing, Qinfeng, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Baojia du-bao heads and deputies were also sent every two years: six from the metropolitan region, four each from Hebei and Hedong, and seven from Yongxing, Qinfeng, and the other circuits.

sentences.zh: 都保正、指揮使與下班殿侍，副保正、副指揮使與三司軍將，正副都頭與守闕軍將，並賜衣及銀帶、銀裹頭杖，給馬有差。

translations.literal: Du-bao heads and commanders received the rank of Attendant of the Lower Hall; deputy heads and deputy commanders the rank of Military Officer of the Three Departments; chief and deputy squad leaders the rank of Awaiting Military Officer—all given robes, silver belts, and silver-headed staffs, with horses granted in varying numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Du-bao heads and commanders were made Attendants of the Lower Hall; deputy heads and deputy commanders Military Officers of the Three Departments; chief and deputy squad leaders Awaiting Military Officers—all received robes, silver belts, and silver-headed staffs, with horses granted in varying numbers.

sentences.zh: 初，保甲隸司農，熙寧八年，改隸兵部，增同判一、主簿二、幹當公事官十，分按諸州，其政令則聽於樞密院。

translations.literal: Initially baojia were subordinate to the Bureau of Agriculture; in the eighth year of Xining they were transferred to the Ministry of War, with one associate administrator, two registrars, and ten clerks added to tour the prefectures; policy orders came from the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At first baojia fell under the Bureau of Agriculture; in the eighth year of Xining they were transferred to the Ministry of War, with one associate administrator, two registrars, and ten clerks added to inspect the prefectures, while policy directives came from the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十年，樞密院副都承旨張誠一上《五路義勇保甲敕》。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Vice Commissioner Zhang Chengyi of the Bureau of Military Affairs presented the Statutes on Yiyong and Baojia of the Five Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Zhang Chengyi, vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, submitted the Statutes on Yiyong and Baojia of the Five Circuits.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，翰林學士、權判尚書兵部許將修《開封府界保甲敕》，成書上之，詔皆頒焉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng, Hanlin Academician and Acting Minister of War Xu Jiang revised the Statutes on Baojia of the Metropolitan Region; when the book was completed and submitted, an edict ordered both promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanfeng, Xu Jiang, Hanlin academician and acting minister of war, revised the Statutes on Baojia of the Metropolitan Region; when the work was completed and submitted, an edict ordered both codes promulgated.

sentences.zh: 二年十一月，始立《府界集教大保長法》，以昭宣使入內內侍省副都知王中正、東上閣門使狄諮兼提舉府界教保甲大保長，總二十二縣為教場十一所，大保長凡二千八百二十五人，每十人一色事藝，置教頭一。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year, the Law on Concentrated Instruction of Large-Bao Chiefs of the Metropolitan Region was first established; Palace Attendant and Vice Director of the Inner Palace Service Wang Zhongzheng and Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner Di Zi were appointed to supervise instruction of metropolitan baojia large-bao chiefs; twenty-two counties formed eleven training grounds with 2,825 large-bao chiefs; every ten men of one specialty had one instructor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year the Law on Concentrated Instruction of Large-Bao Chiefs of the Metropolitan Region was established. Wang Zhongzheng, palace attendant and vice director of the Inner Palace Service, and Di Zi, eastern upper gate commissioner, were appointed to supervise the training of metropolitan large-bao chiefs. Twenty-two counties were organized into eleven training grounds with 2,825 large-bao chiefs in all; every ten men practicing one specialty had one instructor.

sentences.zh: 凡禁軍教頭二百七十，都教頭三十，使臣十。

translations.literal: In all there were 270 instructors from the palace guards, 30 chief instructors, and 10 commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In all there were 270 instructors drawn from the palace guards, 30 chief instructors, and 10 commissioners.

sentences.zh: 弓以八斗、九鬥、一石為三等，弩以二石四斗、二石七斗、三石為三等，馬射九斗、八鬥為二等，其材力超拔者為出等。

translations.literal: For bows, eight, nine, and ten dou were three grades; for crossbows, two piculs four dou, two piculs seven dou, and three piculs were three grades; for mounted archery, nine and eight dou were two grades; those of exceptional strength were above grade.
translations.idiomatic: Bow grades were set at eight, nine, and ten dou; crossbow grades at two piculs four dou, two piculs seven dou, and three piculs; mounted archery at nine and eight dou; men of exceptional strength were classed above grade.

sentences.zh: 當教時，月給錢三千，日給食，官予戎械、戰袍，又具銀楪、酒醪以為賞犒。

translations.literal: During instruction they received three thousand cash monthly, daily food, arms and battle robes from the government, and silver dishes with wine as rewards.
translations.idiomatic: During training they received three thousand cash a month and daily rations, were issued arms and battle robes by the government, and were rewarded with silver dishes and wine.

sentences.zh: 三年，大保長藝成，乃立團教法，以大保長為教頭，教保丁焉。

translations.literal: In the third year, when large-bao chiefs had completed their training, the group-instruction law was established, with large-bao chiefs as instructors teaching bao ding.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, once the large-bao chiefs had completed their training, a group-instruction system was established in which they served as instructors for the bao ding.

sentences.zh: 凡一都保相近者分為五團，即本團都副保正所居空地聚教之。

translations.literal: Nearby du-bao were divided into five groups, gathering for instruction on open ground where the du-bao head or deputy lived.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring du-bao were divided into five groups and assembled for instruction on open ground near the residence of the du-bao head or deputy.

sentences.zh: 以大保長藝成者十人袞教，五日一周之。

translations.literal: Ten trained large-bao chiefs taught in rotation, completing a cycle every five days.
translations.idiomatic: Ten trained large-bao chiefs taught in rotation, completing a cycle every five days.

sentences.zh: 五分其丁，以其一為騎，二為弓，三為弩。

translations.literal: The men were divided five ways: one part mounted, two parts bow, three parts crossbow.
translations.idiomatic: The men were divided into five parts: one part mounted, two parts bow, and three parts crossbow.

sentences.zh: 府界法成，乃推之三路，各置文武官一人提舉，河北則狄諮、劉定，陝西則張山甫，河東則黃廉、王崇拯，以封樁養贍義勇保甲錢糧給其費。

translations.literal: When the metropolitan law was complete, it was extended to the Three Circuits, each with one civil or military official to supervise: Di Zi and Liu Ding for Hebei, Zhang Shanfu for Shaanxi, Huang Lian and Wang Chongzheng for Hedong, funded from sealed-reserve grain and cash for yiyong and baojia support.
translations.idiomatic: Once the metropolitan system was in place it was extended to the Three Circuits, each with one civil or military supervisor—Di Zi and Liu Ding in Hebei, Zhang Shanfu in Shaanxi, Huang Lian and Wang Chongzheng in Hedong—funded from sealed-reserve funds set aside for yiyong and baojia support.

sentences.zh: 是歲，引府界保甲武藝成，帝親閱，錄作能者，餘賜金帛。

translations.literal: That year trained metropolitan baojia were presented; the emperor personally reviewed them, recorded the able, and gave gold and silk to the rest.
translations.idiomatic: That year trained metropolitan baojia were presented; the emperor personally reviewed them, enrolled the most capable, and rewarded the rest with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 四年，改五路義勇為保甲。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, yiyong of the Five Circuits were changed to baojia.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the yiyong of the Five Circuits were reorganized as baojia.

sentences.zh: 狄諮、劉定部領澶州集教大保長四百八十二人見於崇政殿，召執政賜坐閱試，補三班借職、差使、借差凡三十六人，餘賜金帛有差。

translations.literal: Di Zi and Liu Ding led 482 trained large-bao chiefs from Cangzhou to audience in the Hall of Chongzheng; the chief ministers were summoned and given seats to review them; thirty-six were appointed to probationary third-rank posts, dispatch assignments, and temporary assignments; the rest received graded gifts of gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Di Zi and Liu Ding presented 482 trained large-bao chiefs from Cangzhou in the Hall of Chongzheng. The chief ministers were summoned, seated, and asked to review them. Thirty-six men were appointed to probationary third-rank posts, dispatch assignments, or temporary assignments; the rest received graded gifts of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 遷諮四方館使，定集賢校理。

translations.literal: Di Zi was promoted to commissioner of the Four Directions Hostel; Liu Ding to collator of the Hall for the Advancement of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: Di Zi was promoted to commissioner of the Four Directions Hostel and Liu Ding to collator of the Hall for the Advancement of Literature.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：“三路見訓民兵非久，什長藝成，須便行府界團教之，錢糧、官吏並如畿縣，未知及期能辦與不。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "The Three Circuits have trained militia only a short time; when squad leaders complete their training, the metropolitan group-instruction system must at once be applied, with funds, grain, and officials like the metropolitan counties—but it is not known whether this can be completed on schedule."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared: "The Three Circuits have trained their militia only a short while. Once squad leaders complete their training, the metropolitan group-instruction system must immediately be applied there, with funds, grain, and officials arranged as in the metropolitan counties—but it is not yet known whether this can be finished on time."

sentences.zh: 若更稽延日月，必致有誤措置大法，可令承旨取索會校之。

translations.literal: If months are further delayed, the great plan will certainly be mishandled; let the drafting academician gather materials and compare them.
translations.idiomatic: If further months are lost, the great plan will certainly go awry. Let the drafting academician gather the relevant documents and review them together."

sentences.zh: ”其年，府界、河北、河東、陝西路會校保甲，都保凡三千二百六十六，正長、壯丁凡六十九萬一千九百四十五，歲省舊費緡錢一百六十六萬一千四百八十三，歲費緡錢三十一萬三千一百六十六，而團教之賞為錢一百萬有奇不與焉。

translations.literal: "That year the metropolitan region and Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi circuits tallied baojia: 3,266 du-bao in all, 691,945 heads and strong youths; annual old expenses of 1,661,483 strings of cash were saved, annual new expenses were 313,166 strings, while group-instruction rewards of more than one million strings were not included.
translations.idiomatic: "That year the metropolitan region and the Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi circuits tallied their baojia: 3,266 du-bao in all and 691,945 heads and strong youths. Old annual costs of 1,661,483 strings of cash were saved, new annual costs amounted to 313,166 strings, while rewards for group instruction—more than one million strings—were not included in that figure.

sentences.zh: 凡集教、團教成，歲遣使則謂之提舉按閱，率以近臣挾內侍往給賞錢，按格令從事。

translations.literal: Whenever concentrated or group instruction was completed, annual envoys called supervisors of review were sent, usually close ministers accompanied by eunuchs to distribute reward money according to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever concentrated or group instruction was completed, annual envoys called supervisors of review were dispatched, usually close ministers accompanied by eunuchs who distributed reward money according to the regulations.

sentences.zh: 諸路皆以番次藝成者為序，率五六歲一遍，獨河東以金帛不足，乃至十一歲。

translations.literal: All circuits followed the order of those completing training in rotation, generally once every five or six years; only Hedong, for lack of gold and silk, took as long as eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: All circuits followed the order of men completing training in rotation, generally reviewing them once every five or six years; only Hedong, for lack of gold and silk, took as long as eleven years.

sentences.zh: 上以晉人勇悍，介遼、夏間，講勸宜不可後，詔賜緡錢十五萬。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering the people of Jin brave and fierce, situated between Liao and Xia, said encouragement should not be delayed and ordered fifteen thousand strings of cash granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, considering the people of Shanxi brave and warlike and caught between Liao and Xia, said that encouragement must not be delayed and ordered a grant of fifteen thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 時係籍義勇、保甲及民兵凡七百一十八萬二千二十八人雲。

translations.literal: At the time registered yiyong, baojia, and militia totaled 7,182,028 persons.
translations.idiomatic: At that time registered yiyong, baojia, and militia were said to number 7,182,028 men in all.

sentences.zh: （熙寧九年之數。）〉

translations.literal: (Figures for the ninth year of Xining.)
translations.idiomatic: (Figures for the ninth year of Xining.)

sentences.zh: 保甲立法之初，故老大臣皆以為不便，而安石主議甚力，帝卒從之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of baojia legislation, senior ministers all considered it inconvenient, but Anshi advocated it vigorously and the emperor finally followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the baojia laws were first proposed, senior ministers all regarded them as impracticable, but Wang Anshi argued for them with great force and the emperor finally adopted them.

sentences.zh: 今悉著其論難，使來者考焉。

translations.literal: Now all their debates are fully recorded so that later readers may examine them.
translations.idiomatic: Their debates are now fully recorded here so that later readers may judge them.

sentences.zh: 帝嚐論租庸調法而善之，安石對曰：“此法近井田，後世立事粗得先王遺意，則無不善。

translations.literal: The emperor once discussed the zu-yong-diao tax system and praised it; Anshi replied: "This law resembles the well-field system; when later ages establish affairs that roughly capture the former kings' intent, nothing is not good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once discussed the zu-yong-diao tax system and spoke favorably of it. Wang Anshi replied: "That system resembles the well-field ideal. Whenever later ages establish institutions that roughly recover the intent of the former kings, nothing in them is without merit."

sentences.zh: 今亦無不可為。

translations.literal: Today also there is nothing that cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: There is nothing in it that cannot be done today."

sentences.zh: 顧難速成爾。

translations.literal: Only it is hard to complete quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Only it is hard to bring it to completion quickly."

sentences.zh: ”及帝再問，則曰：“人主誠能知天下利害，以其所謂害者製法，而加於兼並之人，則人自不敢保過限之田；

translations.literal: "When the emperor asked again, he said: "If the ruler truly knows the benefits and harms of the realm, makes laws from what is called harm and applies them to those who merge holdings, then people will not dare keep fields beyond the limit;"
translations.idiomatic: "When the emperor asked again, he said: "If the ruler truly understands what benefits and harms the realm, and frames laws from what is harmful and applies them to those who consolidate landholdings, then people will not dare retain fields beyond the limit;"

sentences.zh: 以其所謂利者製法，而加於力耕之人，則人自勸於力耕，而授田不能過限。

translations.literal: makes laws from what is called benefit and applies them to those who labor at farming, then people will encourage themselves in farming, and allotted fields cannot exceed the limit."
translations.idiomatic: if he frames laws from what is beneficial and applies them to those who labor diligently in the fields, then people will encourage themselves to farm diligently, and allotted fields cannot exceed the limit."

sentences.zh: 然此須漸乃能成法。

translations.literal: Yet this must be gradual before it can become law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this can become sound law only if it is carried out gradually."

sentences.zh: 使人主誠知利害之權，因以好惡加之，則所好何患人之不從，所惡何患人之不避？

translations.literal: If the ruler truly knows the power of benefit and harm and applies liking and disliking accordingly, then for what he likes need one fear that people will not follow, or for what he dislikes that they will not avoid?
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler truly grasps the power of benefit and harm and applies his favor and disfavor accordingly, why should he fear that men will not follow what he favors or avoid what he disfavors?"

sentences.zh: 若人主無道以揆之，則多為異議所奪，雖有善法，何由立哉？

translations.literal: If the ruler has no way to measure them, then much is seized by dissenting opinion; even if there is good law, how can it be established?
translations.idiomatic: But if the ruler lacks the means to judge these matters, dissenting opinion will seize control, and even a good law—how can it be established?"

sentences.zh: 帝謂府兵與租庸調法相須，安石則曰：“今義勇、土軍上番供役，既有廩給，則無貧富皆可以入衛出戍，雖無租庸調法，亦自可為。

translations.literal: The emperor said that fubing and the zu-yong-diao system depended on each other; Anshi said: "Today yiyong and local troops on rotating duty with rations provided—rich and poor alike can enter guard service and go on campaign; even without the zu-yong-diao system, it can be done."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said that the fubing system and the zu-yong-diao tax system depended on each other. Wang Anshi replied: "Today, with yiyong and local troops serving in rotating shifts and receiving rations, rich and poor alike can enter guard service and go on campaign. Even without the zu-yong-diao system, this can be done."

sentences.zh: 第義勇皆良民，當以禮義獎養。

translations.literal: Only yiyong are all good commoners and should be encouraged and nurtured with ritual and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: But the yiyong are all good commoners and should be encouraged and nurtured with ritual and righteousness."

sentences.zh: 今皆倒置者，以涅其手背也，教閱而縻費也，使之運糧也。

translations.literal: What is all inverted today is branding their hand-backs, drilling them at wasteful expense, and making them transport grain.
translations.idiomatic: What is turned upside down today is branding recruits on the hand, drilling them at wasteful expense, and making them haul grain.

sentences.zh: 三者皆人所不樂，若更毆之就敵，使被殺戮，尤人所憚也。

translations.literal: All three are what people do not welcome; if in addition they are beaten to face the enemy and made to be slaughtered, that is especially what people dread.
translations.idiomatic: All three are things people hate; if on top of that they are beaten forward against the enemy and sent to be slaughtered, that is what they fear most.

sentences.zh: 馮京曰：“義勇亦有以挽強得試推恩者。

translations.literal: Feng Jing said: "Among the yiyong there are also those who gain trial and imperial grace through draw-strength."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jing said, "Among the yiyong there are also men who win trial and imperial favor through draw-strength."

sentences.zh: ”安石曰：“挽強而力有不足，則絕於進取，是朝廷有推恩之濫。

translations.literal: " Wang Anshi said: "With draw-strength but insufficient strength, advancement is cut off—this is the court's abuse of grace."
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Anshi said, "When draw-strength is tested but strength falls short, advancement is blocked—this is the court's abuse of imperial favor."

sentences.zh: 初非勸獎使人趨武用也。

translations.literal: It was never in the first place encouragement to make people rush toward military use.
translations.idiomatic: That was never meant to encourage men to take up arms in earnest.

sentences.zh: 今欲措置義勇皆當反此，使害在於不為義勇，而利在於為義勇，則俗可變而眾技可成。

translations.literal: Now in arranging the yiyong one should reverse all this, so that harm lies in not being yiyong and benefit lies in being yiyong; then custom can change and many skills can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: In organizing the yiyong we should reverse this: make the harm lie in not serving and the benefit in serving, and custom will change and many skills can be mastered.

sentences.zh: 臣願擇鄉閭豪傑以為將校，稍加獎拔，則人自悅服。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to select village heroes as officers and give them slight rewards and promotion; then people will gladly submit of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: I propose selecting local leaders as officers and giving them modest rewards and promotion; then men will submit willingly.

sentences.zh: 矧今募兵為宿衛，及有積官至刺史以上者。

translations.literal: Moreover, today hired troops serve as palace guards, and some have risen by accumulated rank to regional governor and above.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, hired troops now serve as palace guards, and some have risen through long service to regional governor and above.

sentences.zh: 移此與彼，固無不可，況不至如此費官祿，已足使人樂為哉！

translations.literal: Transferring this to them would certainly be feasible; moreover it would not even reach the point of spending official salaries, yet would suffice to make people glad to serve!
translations.idiomatic: Shifting this role to them is entirely feasible; it need not even cost official salaries, yet would be enough to make men glad to serve!

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能審擇，近臣皆有政事之材，則異時可使分將此等軍矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can truly select carefully, close ministers all have talent for state affairs and in time could be made to command such armies.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty selects carefully, your close ministers all have talent for government and could in time be set to command such forces.

sentences.zh: 今募兵出於無賴之人，尚可為軍、廂主，則近臣以上豈不及此輩，此乃先王成法，社稷之長計也。

translations.literal: Today hired troops come from worthless men, yet they can still serve as army and company commanders; how could close ministers and above not match this lot? This is the enduring law of the former kings and a long-term plan for the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Today's hired troops are drawn from worthless men, yet they can still serve as army and company commanders; are close ministers not their equal? This is the enduring law of the former kings and a long-term plan for the realm."

sentences.zh: ”帝以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought it correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 時有欲以義勇代正兵者，曾公亮以為置義勇、弓手，漸可以省正兵。

translations.literal: At the time some wished to replace regular troops with yiyong; Zeng Gongliang held that establishing yiyong and bowmen could gradually reduce regular troops.
translations.idiomatic: Some then wished to replace regular troops with yiyong. Zeng Gongliang held that establishing yiyong and bowmen could gradually spare regular troops.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：“誠然，第今江、淮置新弓手，適足以傷農。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "That is so; only that establishing new bowmen in the Jianghuai region just now is enough to harm farming."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "That is so, but establishing new bowmen in the Jianghuai region right now would only harm farming."

sentences.zh: ”富弼亦論京西弓手非便。

translations.literal: " Fu Bi also argued that bowmen in the Jingxi circuit were not expedient.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Bi also argued that bowmen in the Jingxi circuit were inexpedient.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：“揆文教，奮武衛，先王所以待遠邇者固不同。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "Weighing civil teaching and rousing martial guard—the way the former kings treated the near and far was certainly not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "Weighing civil teaching against rousing martial guard—the former kings certainly did not treat near and far alike.

sentences.zh: 今處置江、淮與三邊，事當有異。

translations.literal: In handling the Jianghuai and the three border circuits, affairs ought to differ."
translations.idiomatic: In handling the Jianghuai and the three border circuits, policy ought to differ."

sentences.zh: 帝又言節財用，安石對以減兵最急。

translations.literal: The emperor again spoke of economizing expenditures; Anshi answered that reducing troops was most urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again spoke of economizing expenditures. Wang Anshi answered that reducing troops was the most urgent step.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“比慶曆數已甚減矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Compared with the Qingli era the numbers have already been greatly reduced."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Compared with the Qingli era the numbers have already been greatly reduced."

sentences.zh: ”因舉河北、陝西兵數，慮募兵太少，又訓擇不精，緩急或闕事。

translations.literal: He then cited troop numbers in Hebei and Shaanxi, fearing that hired troops were too few and that selection and training were not refined, so that in emergency there might be a shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: He then cited troop numbers in Hebei and Shaanxi, fearing that hired troops were too few and that selection and training were not refined, so that in an emergency affairs might fall short.

sentences.zh: 安石則曰：“精訓練募兵而鼓舞三路之民習兵，則兵可省。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "If hired troops are finely trained and the people of the three circuits are encouraged to practice arms, then troops can be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "If hired troops are finely trained and the people of the three circuits are encouraged to practice arms, troops can be reduced.

sentences.zh: 臣屢言河北舊為武人割據，內抗朝廷，外敵四鄰，亦有禦奚、契丹者，兵儲不外求而足。

translations.literal: Your servant has repeatedly said that in former times Hebei was carved up by military men who resisted the court within and faced neighboring enemies without, and some also resisted the Xi and Khitan; military stores were sufficient without seeking them elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: I have repeatedly said that in former times Hebei was carved up by military men who resisted the court within and faced neighboring enemies without; some also fought the Xi and Khitan, yet military stores were sufficient without outside supply.

sentences.zh: 今河北戶口蕃息，又舉天下財物奉之，常若不足。

translations.literal: Today Hebei's registered households have multiplied, yet the empire's wealth is devoted to them as if it were never enough.
translations.idiomatic: Today Hebei's population has grown, yet the empire's wealth is devoted to it as if it were never enough.

sentences.zh: 以當一面之敵，其施設乃不如武人割據時。

translations.literal: Facing enemies on one front, its arrangements are inferior to when military men held it by force.
translations.idiomatic: Facing enemies on one front, its arrangements are inferior to when military men held it by force.

sentences.zh: 則三路事有當講畫者，在專用其民而已。

translations.literal: Then in the three circuits there are matters that ought to be planned: it lies solely in fully using their people."
translations.idiomatic: Then in the three circuits there are matters that ought to be planned: it lies solely in fully using their people."

sentences.zh: ”帝又言：“邊兵不足以守，徒費衣廩。

translations.literal: The emperor again said: "Border troops are insufficient to defend yet vainly consume clothing and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again said, "Border troops are insufficient to defend yet vainly consume clothing and grain.

sentences.zh: 然固邊圉又不可悉減。

translations.literal: Yet securing the frontier cannot be entirely reduced."
translations.idiomatic: Yet securing the frontier cannot be entirely cut."

sentences.zh: ”安石曰：“今更減兵，即誠無以待急緩；

translations.literal: Anshi said: "If troops are reduced further now, there truly will be nothing to meet emergency;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "If troops are reduced further now, there truly will be nothing to meet emergency;

sentences.zh: 不減，則費財困國無已時。

translations.literal: if not reduced, then wasting wealth and straining the state will have no end.
translations.idiomatic: if they are not reduced, wasting wealth and straining the state will have no end.

sentences.zh: 臣以謂儻不能理兵，稍復古製，則中國無富強之理。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that if troops cannot be managed and the ancient system somewhat restored, then within China there is no principle of wealth and strength."
translations.idiomatic: I hold that if troops cannot be managed and the ancient system somewhat restored, there is no path to wealth and strength within China."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“唐都長安，府兵多在關中，則為強本。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Tang's capital was Chang'an; fubing were mostly in Guanzhong, and thus the root was strong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Tang's capital was Chang'an; fubing were mostly in Guanzhong, and thus the root was strong.

sentences.zh: 今都關東而府兵盛。

translations.literal: Today the capital is east of the Pass yet fubing flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Today the capital is east of the Pass yet fubing flourish.

sentences.zh: 則京師反不足待四方。

translations.literal: Then the capital is on the contrary insufficient to await the four quarters."
translations.idiomatic: Then the capital is on the contrary insufficient to await the four quarters."

sentences.zh: ”安石曰：“府兵在處可為，又可令入衛，則不患本不強。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "Fubing can be stationed locally and can also be ordered into palace guard service; then one need not worry that the root is not strong."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "Fubing can be stationed locally and can also be ordered into palace guard service; then one need not worry that the root is not strong."

sentences.zh: ”韓絳、呂公弼皆以入衛為難。

translations.literal: Han Jiang and Lü Gongbi both held that entering guard service was difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jiang and Lü Gongbi both held that entering guard service was difficult.

sentences.zh: 文彥博曰：“ 如曹、濮人專為盜賊，豈宜使入衛？

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo said: "Men of Cao and Pu specialize in being bandits—how can they be made to enter guard service?"
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo said, "Men of Cao and Pu specialize in being bandits—how can they be made to enter guard service?"

sentences.zh: ”安石曰：“曹、濮人豈無應募？

translations.literal: " Anshi said: "Are there not men of Cao and Pu who answer recruitment?
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Anshi said, "Are there not men of Cao and Pu who answer recruitment?

sentences.zh: 皆暴猾無賴之人，尚不以為虞；

translations.literal: They are all violent and worthless men, yet they are not regarded as a concern;
translations.idiomatic: They are all violent and worthless men, yet they are not regarded as a concern;

sentences.zh: 義勇皆良民，又以物力戶為將校，豈當復以為可虞也？

translations.literal: the yiyong are all good commoners, and officers are chosen from households by property—how can they again be regarded as a concern?"
translations.idiomatic: the yiyong are all good commoners, and officers are chosen from households by property—how can they again be regarded as a concern?"

sentences.zh: 陳升之欲令義勇以漸戍近州。

translations.literal: Chen Shengzhi wished to have yiyong gradually garrison nearby prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shengzhi wished to have yiyong gradually garrison nearby prefectures.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：“陛下若欲去數百年募兵之敝，則宜果斷，詳立法製，令本末備具。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "If Your Majesty wishes to remove the evils of hired troops accumulated over hundreds of years, then one should be resolute, carefully establish laws and institutions, and make root and branch complete.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "If Your Majesty wishes to remove the evils of hired troops accumulated over hundreds of years, you should be resolute, carefully establish laws and institutions, and make root and branch complete.

sentences.zh: 不然，無補也。

translations.literal: Otherwise there is no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise there is no benefit."

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“製而用之，在法當預立條製，以漸推行。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "To make institutions and use them—in law one should pre-establish regulations and gradually carry them out."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "To make institutions and use them—in law one should pre-establish regulations and gradually carry them out."

sentences.zh: ”彥博等又以為土兵難使千里出戍。

translations.literal: Yanbo and others again held that local militia were hard to make travel a thousand li on garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo and others again held that local militia were hard to make travel a thousand li on garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：“前代征流求，討党項，豈非府兵乎？

translations.literal: Anshi said: "In former ages when they campaigned against Liuqiu and the Tangut, were these not fubing?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "In former ages when they campaigned against Liuqiu and the Tangut, were these not fubing?"

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“募兵專於戰守，故可恃；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Hired troops specialize in fighting and defense and thus can be relied on;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Hired troops specialize in fighting and defense and thus can be relied on;

sentences.zh: 至民兵，則兵農之業相半，可恃以戰守乎？

translations.literal: as for militia, then military and farming occupations are half and half—can they be relied on for fighting and defense?"
translations.idiomatic: as for militia, military and farming are half and half—can they be relied on for fighting and defense?"

sentences.zh: ”安石曰：“唐以前未有黥兵，然亦可以戰守。

translations.literal: " Anshi said: "Before Tang there were no tattooed troops, yet they could also fight and defend.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Anshi said, "Before Tang there were no tattooed troops, yet they could also fight and defend.

sentences.zh: 臣以謂募兵與民兵無異，顧所用將帥如何爾。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that hired troops and militia are not different; it depends solely on what generals are used.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that hired troops and militia are not different; it depends solely on what generals are used.

sentences.zh: 將帥非難求，但人主能察見群臣情偽，善駕禦之，則人材出而為用，不患無將帥。

translations.literal: Generals are not hard to seek; only the ruler must discern the truth and falsity of his ministers' feelings and skillfully drive them; then talent emerges for use and one need not worry about lacking generals.
translations.idiomatic: Generals are not hard to find; only the ruler must discern his ministers' truth and falsity and skillfully drive them—then talent emerges for use and one need not worry about lacking generals.

sentences.zh: 有將帥，則不患民兵不為用矣。

translations.literal: With generals, one need not worry that militia will not be used."
translations.idiomatic: With generals, one need not worry that militia will not be used."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“經遠之策，必至什伍其民，費省而兵眾，且與募兵相為用矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The policy of reaching afar must ultimately organize the people in groups of ten and five, economizing expense while multiplying troops, and use them together with hired troops."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The policy of reaching afar must ultimately organize the people in groups of ten and five, economizing expense while multiplying troops, and use them together with hired troops."

sentences.zh: ”安石對曰：“欲公私財用不匱，為宗社長久計，募兵水法誠當變革。

translations.literal: " Anshi answered: "If public and private wealth are not to be exhausted and a long-term plan made for the altars of state, the hired-troop water law truly ought to be reformed."
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Anshi answered, "If public and private wealth are not to be exhausted and a long-term plan made for the altars of state, the hired-troop system truly ought to be reformed."

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“密院以為必有建中之變。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Bureau of Military Affairs holds that there will surely be a Jianzhong-era upheaval."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Bureau of Military Affairs holds that there will surely be a Jianzhong-era upheaval."

sentences.zh: ”安石對曰：“陛下躬行德義，憂勤政事，上下不蔽，必無此理。

translations.literal: Anshi answered: "Your Majesty personally practices virtue and righteousness, worries and labors at government, and above and below are not blocked—surely there is no such principle.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi answered, "Your Majesty personally practices virtue and righteousness, worries and labors at government, and above and below are not blocked—surely there is no such principle.

sentences.zh: 建中所以致變，德宗用盧杞之徒而疏陸贄，其不亡者幸也。

translations.literal: The reason Jianzhong brought upheaval was that Dezong employed men like Lu Qi and kept Lu Zhi at a distance; that it did not perish was fortune."
translations.idiomatic: The reason Jianzhong brought upheaval was that Dezong employed men like Lu Qi and kept Lu Zhi at a distance; that the dynasty did not perish was fortune."

sentences.zh: 時開封鞫保戶有質衣而買弓箭者，帝恐其貧乏，難於出備。

translations.literal: At the time Kaifeng was investigating baojia households who had pawned clothing to buy bows and arrows; the emperor feared their poverty and difficulty in providing equipment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Kaifeng was investigating baojia households who had pawned clothing to buy bows and arrows; the emperor feared their poverty and difficulty in providing equipment.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：“民貧宜有之，抑民使置弓箭，則法所弗去也。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "It is fitting that the people be poor; restraining the people to make them provide bows and arrows is what the law does not remove.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "It is fitting that some among the people be poor; pressing the people to provide bows and arrows is what the law does not set aside.

sentences.zh: 往者冬閱及巡檢番上，唯就用在官弓矢，不知百姓何故至於質衣也。

translations.literal: In former times winter review and rotating patrol duty used only official bows and arrows on hand; your servant does not know why the common people came to pawn clothing.
translations.idiomatic: In former times winter review and rotating patrol duty used only official bows and arrows on hand; I do not know why the common people came to pawn clothing.

sentences.zh: 然自生民以來。

translations.literal: Yet from the birth of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the birth of the people.

sentences.zh: 兵農為一，耒耜以養生，弓矢以免死，皆凡民所宜自具，未有造耒耜、弓矢以給百姓者也。

translations.literal: Military and farming were one: plow and hoe to sustain life, bow and arrow to escape death—both were what common people ought to provide for themselves; never were plow, hoe, bow, and arrow made to supply the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Military and farming were one: plow and hoe to sustain life, bow and arrow to escape death—both were what common people ought to provide for themselves; never were plow, hoe, bow, and arrow manufactured to supply the common people.

sentences.zh: 然則雖使百姓置弓矢，亦不為過。

translations.literal: Then even making the common people provide bows and arrows is not excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Then even making the common people provide bows and arrows is not excessive.

sentences.zh: 第陛下優恤百姓甚至，故今立法，一聽民便爾。

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty is extremely gracious in cherishing the common people, and so in legislating today one listens entirely to the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Only Your Majesty is extremely gracious in cherishing the common people, and so in legislating today one listens entirely to the people's convenience.

sentences.zh: 且府界素多群盜，攻劫殺掠，一歲之間至二百火，逐火皆有賞錢，備賞之人即今保丁也。

translations.literal: Moreover, within the capital district there have always been many bandit gangs; in one year plunder and killing reached two hundred fires, and for each fire there was reward money—the men who prepared the reward are today's baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, within the capital district there have always been many bandit gangs; in one year plunder and killing reached two hundred incidents, and for each incident there was reward money—the men who prepared the reward are today's baoding.

sentences.zh: 方其備賞之時，豈無賣易衣服以納官賞者？

translations.literal: When they prepared the reward, were there not those who sold or exchanged clothing to pay the official reward?
translations.idiomatic: When they prepared the reward, were there not those who sold or exchanged clothing to pay the official reward?

sentences.zh: 然人皆以謂賞錢宜出於百姓。

translations.literal: Yet everyone held that reward money ought to come from the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet everyone held that reward money ought to come from the common people.

sentences.zh: 夫出錢之多不足以止盜，而保甲之能止盜，其效已見，則雖令民出少錢以置器械，未有損也。

translations.literal: That much money spent could not stop bandits, while baojia's power to stop bandits has already been seen in effect; then even ordering the people to spend a little money to provide weapons has not harmed them.
translations.idiomatic: That much money spent could not stop bandits, while baojia's power to stop bandits has already been seen in effect; then even ordering the people to spend a little money to provide weapons has not harmed them.

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“賞錢人所習慣，則安之如自然；

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Reward money is what people are accustomed to, and they accept it as natural;
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Reward money is what people are accustomed to, and they accept it as natural;

sentences.zh: 不習慣，則不能無怨。

translations.literal: what they are not accustomed to, they cannot be without complaint.
translations.idiomatic: what they are not accustomed to, they cannot be without complaint.

sentences.zh: 如何決壞民產，民不怨；

translations.literal: How is it that breaking dikes harms the people's property yet the people do not complain;
translations.idiomatic: How is it that breaking dikes harms the people's property yet the people do not complain;

sentences.zh: 決河以壞民產，則怨矣。

translations.literal: breaking rivers to harm the people's property, and they complain?"
translations.idiomatic: breaking rivers to harm the people's property, and they complain?"

sentences.zh: 帝嚐批：“陳留縣所行保甲，每十人一小保，中三人或五人須要弓箭，縣吏督責，無者有刑。

translations.literal: The emperor once annotated: "The baojia carried out in Chenliu County: every ten men make one small bao; of them three or five must have bows and arrows; county clerks supervise and demand, and those without them are punished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once annotated, "The baojia carried out in Chenliu County: every ten men make one small bao; of them three or five must have bows and arrows; county clerks supervise and demand, and those without them are punished.

sentences.zh: 百姓買一弓至千五百，十箭至六七百，當青黃不接之際，貧下客丁安能出辦？

translations.literal: The common people pay up to 1,500 for one bow and six or seven hundred for ten arrows; in the season when green and yellow do not connect, how can poor guest households and ding provide them?
translations.idiomatic: The common people pay up to 1,500 cash for one bow and six or seven hundred for ten arrows; in the season when green and yellow do not connect, how can poor guest households and ding provide them?

sentences.zh: 又每一小保用民力築射垛，又自辦錢糧起鋪屋。

translations.literal: Moreover each small bao uses civilian labor to build shooting platforms, and they themselves provide money and grain to erect shed buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover each small bao uses civilian labor to build shooting platforms, and they themselves provide money and grain to erect shed buildings.

sentences.zh: 每保置鼓，遇賊聲擊，民居遠近不一，甲家遭賊，鼓在乙家，則無緣聲擊。

translations.literal: Each bao sets up a drum; when bandits come they strike it, but dwellings are near and far and not uniform—when household A meets bandits and the drum is at household B, there is no way to strike it in time.
translations.idiomatic: Each bao sets up a drum; when bandits come they strike it, but dwellings are near and far and not uniform—when household A meets bandits and the drum is at household B, there is no way to strike it in time.

sentences.zh: 如此，須人置一鼓，費錢不少。

translations.literal: Thus each person would need one drum, and the expense in cash would be considerable.
translations.idiomatic: Thus each person would need one drum, and the expense in cash would be considerable.

sentences.zh: 可速指揮令止如元議，團保覺察盜賊，餘無得施行。

translations.literal: Order quickly that it stop as originally discussed: group bao to detect bandits, and nothing else may be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Order quickly that it stop as originally discussed: group bao to detect bandits, and nothing else may be carried out.

sentences.zh: 鄉民既憂無錢買弓箭，加以傳惑徙之戍邊，是以父子聚首號泣者非虛也。

translations.literal: Villagers already worry about lacking money to buy bows and arrows, and in addition rumors confuse them about transfer to border garrison—thus fathers and sons gathering to wail is not empty.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers already worry about lacking money to buy bows and arrows, and in addition rumors confuse them about transfer to border garrison—thus fathers and sons gathering to wail is not empty.

sentences.zh: ”安石進呈不行。

translations.literal: " Anshi presented this and it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Anshi presented this and it was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 帝謂安石：“保甲誠有斬指者，此事宜緩而密。

translations.literal: The emperor told Anshi: "Baojia truly has those who cut off fingers; this matter should be slow and secret."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Wang Anshi, "Baojia truly has those who cut off fingers; this matter should be slow and secret."

sentences.zh: ”安石曰：“日力可惜。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "Days' strength is precious."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "Days' strength is precious."

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“然亦不可遽，恐卻沮事。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yet one also cannot be hasty, for fear of discouraging the affair."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yet one also cannot be hasty, for fear of discouraging the affair."

sentences.zh: ”安石曰：“此事自不敢不密。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "In this matter your servant dares not be other than secret."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "In this matter I dare not be other than secret."

sentences.zh: ”權知開封府韓維等言：“諸縣團結保甲，鄉民驚擾。

translations.literal: " Acting Kaifeng prefect Han Wei and others said: "In all counties group baojia; villagers are alarmed and disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: " Acting Kaifeng prefect Han Wei and others said, "In all counties group baojia; villagers are alarmed and disturbed.

sentences.zh: 祥符等縣已畢，其餘縣乞候農閑排定。

translations.literal: Xiangfu and other counties are already finished; the remaining counties beg to wait until the farming slack season to arrange them."
translations.idiomatic: Xiangfu and other counties are already finished; the remaining counties beg to wait until the farming slack season to arrange them."

sentences.zh: ”時府界諸縣鄉民，或自殘傷以避團結。

translations.literal: At the time in all counties of the capital district, some villagers maimed themselves to avoid grouping.
translations.idiomatic: At the time in all counties of the capital district, some villagers maimed themselves to avoid grouping.

sentences.zh: 安石辨說甚力。

translations.literal: Anshi argued forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi argued forcefully.

sentences.zh: 時曾孝寬為府界提點，榜募告捕扇惑保甲者雖甚嚴，有匿名書封丘郭門者，於是詔重賞捕之。

translations.literal: At the time Zeng Xiaokuan was capital-district intendant; he posted rewards to report and capture those who incited baojia though very strict, yet there was an anonymous letter sealed at the Fengqiu city gate; therefore an edict offered heavy reward for capture.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zeng Xiaokuan was capital-district intendant; he posted rewards to report and capture those who incited baojia though very strict, yet there was an anonymous letter sealed at the Fengqiu city gate; therefore an edict offered heavy reward for capture.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：“乃者保甲，人得其願上番狀，然後使之，宜於人情無所驚疑。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "Recently in baojia, people obtained the petition they wished to submit for rotating duty, and only then were they made to serve—this should cause no alarm or doubt in human feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "Recently in baojia, people obtained the petition they wished to submit for rotating duty, and only then were they made to serve—this should cause no alarm or doubt in human feelings.

sentences.zh: 且今居藏盜賊及為盜賊之人，固不便新法。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who harbor bandits and those who are bandits are naturally ill-disposed toward the new law.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those who harbor bandits and those who are bandits are naturally ill-disposed toward the new law.

sentences.zh: 陛下觀長社一縣，捕獲府界劇賊為保甲迫逐出外者至三十人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty observed one county, Changshe: those captured as major bandits of the capital district driven out by baojia pursuit numbered thirty men.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty observed one county, Changshe: those captured as major bandits of the capital district driven out by baojia pursuit numbered thirty men.

sentences.zh: 此曹既不容京畿，又見捕於輔郡，其計無聊，專務扇惑。

translations.literal: This lot, unable to remain in the capital region and seeing capture in the auxiliary commanderies, have no recourse in their schemes and specialize in incitement.
translations.idiomatic: This lot, unable to remain in the capital region and seeing capture in the auxiliary commanderies, have no recourse in their schemes and specialize in incitement.

sentences.zh: 比聞為首扇惑者已就捕，然至京師亦止有二十許人。

translations.literal: Recently it was heard that the chief inciters have been captured, yet upon reaching the capital there are only about twenty men.
translations.idiomatic: Recently it was heard that the chief inciters have been captured, yet upon reaching the capital there are only about twenty men.

sentences.zh: 以十七縣十數萬家，而被扇惑者才二十許人，不可謂多。

translations.literal: Among seventeen counties and tens of thousands of households, those incited number only about twenty men—it cannot be called many.
translations.idiomatic: Among seventeen counties and tens of thousands of households, those incited number only about twenty men—it cannot be called many.

sentences.zh: 自古作事，未有不以勢率眾而能令上下如一者。

translations.literal: Since antiquity in undertaking affairs, never has one not led the multitude by authority and made above and below as one.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity in undertaking affairs, never has one not led the multitude by authority and made above and below as one.

sentences.zh: 今聯十數萬人為保甲，又待其應募乃使之番上，比乃以陛下矜恤之至。

translations.literal: Today linking tens of thousands of men as baojia and waiting until they answer recruitment before making them rotate on duty—this is due to Your Majesty's utmost compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Today linking tens of thousands of men as baojia and waiting until they answer recruitment before making them rotate on duty—this is due to Your Majesty's utmost compassion.

sentences.zh: 令保甲番上捕盜，若任其自去來，即孰肯聽命？

translations.literal: If baojia rotate to capture bandits and they are left free to come and go, who would willingly obey orders?
translations.idiomatic: If baojia rotate to capture bandits and they are left free to come and go, who would willingly obey orders?

sentences.zh: 若以法驅之，又非人所願。

translations.literal: If they are driven by law, that again is not what people wish.
translations.idiomatic: If they are driven by law, that again is not what people wish.

sentences.zh: 且為天下者，如止欲任民情所願而已，則何必立君而為之張官置吏也？

translations.literal: Moreover, for one who holds the realm, if one only wishes to follow what the people's feelings desire, why establish a ruler and set up officials for him?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for one who holds the realm, if one only wishes to follow what the people's feelings desire, why establish a ruler and set up officials for him?

sentences.zh: 今輔郡保甲，宜先遣官諭上旨，後以法推行之。

translations.literal: Now in the auxiliary commanderies' baojia, one should first send officials to announce the imperial intent, then carry out the law.
translations.idiomatic: Now in the auxiliary commanderies' baojia, one should first send officials to announce the imperial intent, then carry out the law.

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“然。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "So."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "So."

sentences.zh: 一日，帝謂安石曰：“曾孝寬言，民有斬指訴保甲者。

translations.literal: One day the emperor told Anshi: "Zeng Xiaokuan says the people have cut off fingers to complain of baojia."
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor told Wang Anshi, "Zeng Xiaokuan says the people have cut off fingers to complain of baojia."

sentences.zh: ”安石曰：“此事得於蔡駰。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "This matter was obtained from Cai Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "This matter was obtained from Cai Yu."

sentences.zh: 趙子幾使駰驗問，乃民因斫木誤斬指，參證者數人。

translations.literal: Zhao Ziji sent Yu to verify; it turned out the people cut off a finger by mistake while chopping wood, and several men testified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ziji sent Yu to verify; it turned out the people cut off a finger by mistake while chopping wood, and several men testified.

sentences.zh: 大抵保甲法，上自執政大臣，中則兩製，下則盜賊及停藏之人，皆所不欲。

translations.literal: Generally the baojia law—from chief ministers above, through two-office men in the middle, down to bandits and those who harbor them—is what none wish.
translations.idiomatic: Generally the baojia law—from chief ministers above, through two-office men in the middle, down to bandits and those who harbor them—is what none wish.

sentences.zh: 然臣召鄉人問之，皆以為便。

translations.literal: Yet your servant summoned villagers to ask them, and all held it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I summoned villagers to ask them, and all held it convenient.

sentences.zh: 則雖有斬指以避丁者，不皆然也。

translations.literal: Then though there are those who cut off fingers to avoid ding, it is not all so.
translations.idiomatic: Then though there are those who cut off fingers to avoid ding, it is not all so.

sentences.zh: 況保甲非特除盜，固可漸習為兵。

translations.literal: Moreover baojia is not solely for eliminating bandits; it can gradually be practiced as troops.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover baojia is not solely for eliminating bandits; it can gradually be practiced as troops.

sentences.zh: 既人皆能射，又為旗鼓變其耳目，且約以免稅上番代巡檢兵；

translations.literal: When all can shoot and banners and drums change their ears and eyes, and moreover they are promised tax exemption for rotating in place of patrol troops;
translations.idiomatic: When all can shoot and banners and drums change their ears and eyes, and moreover they are promised tax exemption for rotating in place of patrol troops;

sentences.zh: 又自正、長而上，能捕賊者獎之以官，則人競勸。

translations.literal: and from zheng and zhang upward, those who can capture bandits are rewarded with office, then people will compete in encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: and from zheng and zhang upward, those who can capture bandits are rewarded with office, then people will compete in encouragement.

sentences.zh: 然後使與募兵相參，則可以銷募兵驕誌，且省財費，此宗社長久之計。

translations.literal: Then make them participate together with hired troops, and hired troops' arrogant will can be dissolved and expenses saved—this is a long-term plan for the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Then make them participate together with hired troops, and hired troops' arrogant will can be dissolved and expenses saved—this is a long-term plan for the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 帝謂什伍百姓如保甲，恐難成，不如便團結成指揮，以使臣管轄。

translations.literal: The emperor said organizing the people in groups of ten like baojia would be hard to accomplish; better to group them at once as command and have commissioners administer them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said organizing the people in groups of ten like baojia would be hard to accomplish; better to group them at once as command and have commissioners administer them.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：“陛下誠能果斷，不恤人言，即便團結指揮，亦無所妨。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "If Your Majesty can truly be resolute and not spare people's words, even grouping command at once would do no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "If Your Majesty can truly be resolute and not spare people's words, even grouping command at once would do no harm.

sentences.zh: 然指揮是虛名，五百人為一保，緩急可喚集，雖不名為指揮，與指揮使無異，乃是實事。

translations.literal: Yet command is an empty name; five hundred men make one bao, and in emergency they can be summoned—though not named command, it is no different from a command envoy; this is a real affair.
translations.idiomatic: Yet command is an empty name; five hundred men make one bao, and in emergency they can be summoned—though not named command, it is no different from a command envoy; this is a real affair.

sentences.zh: 幸不至大急，即免令人駭擾而事集為上策。

translations.literal: Fortunately if there is no great urgency, avoiding alarming the people while affairs are gathered is the best policy."
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately if there is no great urgency, avoiding alarming the people while affairs are gathered is the best policy."

sentences.zh: ”帝遂變三路義勇如府畿保甲法。

translations.literal: The emperor then changed yiyong in the three circuits to match the capital-district baojia law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then changed yiyong in the three circuits to match the capital-district baojia law.

sentences.zh: 馮京曰：“義勇已有指揮使，指揮使即其鄉里豪傑。

translations.literal: Feng Jing said: "Yiyong already have command envoys; command envoys are their village heroes.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jing said, "Yiyong already have command envoys; command envoys are their village heroes.

sentences.zh: 今復作保甲，令何人為大保長？

translations.literal: Now baojia is made again—whom shall be made large-bao chief?"
translations.idiomatic: Now baojia is made again—whom shall be made large-bao chief?"

sentences.zh: ”安石曰：“古者民居則為鄉，伍家為比，比有長，及用兵，即五人為伍，伍有伍司馬。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "In antiquity when people dwelt they formed xiang; five households made bi, and bi had chiefs; when using troops, five men made wu and wu had wu sima.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "In antiquity when people dwelt they formed xiang; five households made bi, and bi had chiefs; when using troops, five men made wu and wu had wu sima.

sentences.zh: 二十五家為閭，閭有閭胥，二十五人為兩，兩有兩司馬。

translations.literal: Twenty-five households made lü, and lü had lü xu; twenty-five men made liang, and liang had liang sima.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five households made lü, and lü had lü xu; twenty-five men made liang, and liang had liang sima.

sentences.zh: 兩司馬即閭胥，伍司馬即比長，第隨事異名而已。

translations.literal: Liang sima is lü xu, wu sima is bi chief—only the names differ with the affair.
